# Draft:"King of Cool's" Impact on Delivery Distribution

"King of Cool's" Impact on Delivery Distribution
Frederick McKinley Jones was born on May 17, 1893 in Cinncinati, Ohio. He is a self-made and self-taught engineer, who later became an entrepreneur, who created the first ever working mobile refrigeration system in trucks, dubbing him the "King of Cool". Jones also served time in the U.S army during World War I and was highly regarding for his mechinal knowledge and experience. After his time in the military, Jones would then partner up with Joseph Numero and be the first ones to invented mobile cooling units in trucks in 1938, and would later patent mobile refrigeration in July 1940.
Due to his outstanding achievement in mobile refrigeration, Jones would become an inductee for both the National and Minnesotas Inventors Hall of Fame. He also had a long-time fascination for race cars, as he was widely regarded as one of the finest mechanics in Great Lakes.  Jones may have passed away on February 21, 1961 in Minneapolis, Minnesota, but his lifes work still lives on to this day as his invention allows for distributors to preserve fresh products, such as fruits, vegetables, livestock, etc. during deliveries, thus giving consumers higher quality food.
